text:
rachel: Quick flag: discovered odd generator behavior in Go SDK when ctx is cancelled while credentials trigger a blocking refresh. Minimal repro below and a proposed shim idea.

rachel: ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
creds := &blockingCreds{delay: 4 * time.Second}
client := NewClient(WithCredentials(creds))

g, _ := client.Generator(ctx, "mini-model")
go func() { time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
if _, err := g.Stream(ctx); err != nil { log.Printf("stream err: %v", err) }
// observed: handshake goroutine blocks in creds.Fetch and never sees ctx.Done() until creds return
```

tom: Repro'd locally. It looks like the handshake path calls creds synchronously without passing the ctx, so a slow refresh blocks cancellation.

anita: Short-term DX: we can add a client option HandshakeTimeout (default 5s) and update onboarding sample to use context.WithTimeout around stream start. Long-term: change Creds interface to GetToken(ctx).

kevin: Compatibility note: changing the interface breaks existing custom creds. Suggest a small shim: if old creds doesn't implement GetToken(ctx), wrap it with a goroutine that performs token fetch but selects on ctx and returns an error if ctx.Done() fires. That avoids leaking the generator handshake goroutine.

rachel: Nice. Proposal: land 1) handshake timeout client option + onboarding doc update, 2) compatibility shim + unit test simulating blocking creds + cancel, 3) next sprint RFC to require GetToken(ctx) for parity with Python/Node.

daniel: (dev-bot) E2E canary noticed generator goroutine increase on private-e2e; filing INF-4512.

anita: For the shim, also document behavior: when ctx cancels we should return a dedicated error type (e.g., ErrAuthCanceled) so apps can distinguish it from auth failures. Update CHANGELOG migration notes.

tom: I'll draft the shim PR + unit test that asserts no goroutine leak and that Stream() returns promptly with ErrAuthCanceled when creds block.

rachel: Thanks. I'll add a short sample-app snippet in the onboarding README showing both the context timeout pattern and how to call g.Abort() if we add that API. Tagging SDK parity triage.

kevin: One more UX thought: show a diagnostic message in the error suggesting "check custom credentials for blocking I/O and prefer GetToken(ctx)" so users can self-diagnose.

rachel: Good call. Done for now.
